_meta.rule: HOTLINES: NEVER add or edit a hotline/text-line number without a human verifying it against an authoritative source (source=national_verified, verified=true). EMERGENCY numbers (police/ambulance/fire): emitted only under the owner's cited-sources standard of 2026-10-29 — >=2 independent agreeing sources, >=1 official, source=multi_source_cited (CIRISAgent#1248). A wrong crisis number is catastrophically worse than the directory fallback.

verification_notes: No human-verified national hotline entries for this locale yet — international directories only. See CRISIS_RESOURCES_VERIFICATION_NEEDED.md before adding entries; numbers require human verification (verified=true) against an authoritative source. Emergency (police/ambulance/fire) numbers for DE, AT, CH added 2026-10-29 (CIRISAgent#1248): 8 of 8 meet the owner's cited-sources standard (source=multi_source_cited, emitted); the rest are staged verified=false and NOT emitted — see CRISIS_RESOURCES_VERIFICATION_NEEDED.md.

emergency_germany_112.name: Emergency services
emergency_germany_112.description: Unified emergency number (ambulance, fire; EU 112 also reaches police)
emergency_germany_112.validation_notes: CITED 2026-10-29 (CIRISAgent#1248) under the owner's cited-sources standard (>=2 independent agreeing sources, >=1 official; no human check). Sources: UK FCDO travel advice: UK FCDO travel advice, Getting help: "Emergency services in Germany Ambulance: 112 Fire: 112 Police: 110" (fetched 2026-10-29 via gov.uk content API) | Ministerium des Inneren, für Digitalisierung und Kommunen Baden-Württemberg: "FEUERWEHR UND RETTUNGSDIENST Bei Bränden, Unglücksfällen und bei lebensbedrohlichen Verletzungen oder medizinischen Notfällen. 112" (https://im.baden-wuerttemberg.de/fileadmin/redaktion/m-im/intern/dateien/pdf/MIDK_Flyer_Notfallnummern_A4_p2.pdf) | AOSP eccdata (Android's emergency-number database): DE 112 types ['AMBULANCE', 'FIRE', 'POLICE']. Sources agree it reaches: ambulance, fire, police. UK FCDO page checked: https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/germany/getting-help (fetched 2026-10-29); page text: UK FCDO travel advice, Getting help: "Emergency services in Germany Ambulance: 112 Fire: 112 Police: 110" (fetched 2026-10-29 via gov.uk content API). Cross-check (not a source): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_emergency_telephone_numbers — wikipedia agrees; EU 112 page confirms 112 works EU-wide. 'languages' = the locale this entry is staged for (de), not a verified statement of operator languages.
